'''Pelle Gustav Gösta Larsson''' (born 23 February 2001)<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelle Larsson|url=https://www.nbadraft.net/players/pelle-larson/|website=NBADraft.net|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> is a Swedish professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Miami Heat]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]] and the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]].

==Early life and career==
Larsson grew up in [[Stockholm]], Sweden, and is the son of Christian Larsson, a former member of the [[Sweden men's national basketball team]].<ref name="auto">{{cite web|first=Brendan|last=Quinn|title=It’s Pelle Larsson’s turn to step into the light at Arizona|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/3929849/2022/12/13/pelle-larsson-arizona/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=13 December 2022|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=John|last=Marshall|title=Pelle Larsson putting his body on the line every game for No. 5 Arizona|url=https://apnews.com/article/arizona-basketball-pelle-larsson-505982bcde4e2b21d7b6ff2df2671e64|website=APNews.com|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=15 February 2024|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> As a youth, he played for the local [[Skuru IK]] basketball team before moving north at age 16 to join [[BC Luleå]].<ref>{{cite news|first=Josh|last=Newman|title=Utah basketball’s Pelle Larsson at the forefront of Runnin’ Utes’ overseas movement|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2021/01/03/utah-basketballs-pelle/|newspaper=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=3 January 2021|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> He played two seasons with [[RIG Luleå]] and BC Luleå in the [[Swedish Basketball League]], being named the league's star of the year in his first season at the top level with averages of 7.6 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.9 assists and 0.8 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Scheer|title=Highlights: Utah transfer Pelle Larsson|url=https://247sports.com/college/duke/article/utah-transfer-pelle-larsson-highlights-arizona-kansas-165184161/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=8 May 2021|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Drew|first=Jay|title=Freshman guard Pelle Larsson, a Swedish import, making instant impact for struggling Utes|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2021/1/13/22228870/utes-basketball-stanford-hoops-pelle-larsson-larry-krystkowiak-branden-carlson-alfonso-plummer|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|date=13 January 2021|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
Larsson moved to the United States in 2020 to play for the [[Utah Utes men's basketball|Utah Utes]].<ref name="auto"/> He became a starter seven games into his [[freshman]] season and averaged 8.2 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 2.8 assists per game; he was 50.0% on 3-point field goals in conference games which was the third-best in the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]], and he was second in the conference with 88.3% of his free throws made.<ref>{{cite news|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=New transfer Pelle Larsson brings shooting touch, physical game to Wildcats|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/new-transfer-pelle-larsson-brings-shooting-touch-physical-game-to-wildcats/article_90132fb0-b0e8-11eb-bcc5-079464c71bd1.html|newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=9 May 2021|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> He announced a transfer to [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] following his only season at Utah.<ref>{{cite news|first=Josh|last=Newman|title=Utah hoops star freshman Pelle Larsson commits to Arizona after entering NCAA Transfer Portal|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/utah-utes/2021/05/09/utah-hoops-star-freshman/|newspaper=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=9 May 2021|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

In his first season at Arizona, 2021–22, Larsson was named the Pac-12 Sixth Man of the Year and appeared in all 37 games, averaging 7.2 points, 3.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelle Larsson|url=https://arizonawildcats.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/pelle-larsson/15372|work=[[Arizona Wildcats]]|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> He played in all 35 games and had 18 starts in 2022–23, averaging 9.9 points and 4.3 rebounds per game.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Scheer|title=Pelle Larsson enters NBA Draft|url=https://247sports.com/college/arizona/article/arizona-pelle-larsson-nab-draft-208977496/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=25 April 2023|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref> He initially entered the [[2023 NBA draft]] but later announced he was returning to Arizona for his [[Senior (education)|senior]] year in 2023–24.<ref>{{cite news|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=Pelle Larsson confirms he will return to Arizona Wildcats for 2023-24 season|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/pelle-larsson-confirms-he-will-return-to-arizona-wildcats-for-2023-24-season/article_3ffdf5b4-f3ad-11ed-9ecd-67aa9dc0ad36.html|newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=16 May 2023|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On 27 June 2024, Larsson was selected with the 44th overall pick by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]], however, immediately on draft night, he was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in exchange for [[AJ Griffin (basketball)|AJ Griffin]] via a three-way trade with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT ACQUIRE PELLE LARSSON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-pelle-larsson|website=NBA.com|date=27 June 2024|access-date=28 June 2024}}</ref> On July 2, he signed with Miami<ref>{{cite web|title=HEAT SIGN PELLE LARSSON|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-sign-pelle-larsson|website=NBA.com|date=2 July 2024|access-date=2 July 2024}}</ref> and on 23 October 2024, he made his NBA debut in a 116–97 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]], scoring two points.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic at Miami Heat Box Score, October 23, 2024|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202410230MIA.html|website=Basketball-Reference.com|date=28 October 2024|access-date=28 October 2024}}</ref> On 2 February 2025, he was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] to the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]]. He was subsequently recalled to the [[Miami Heat]] a day later, on 3 February 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-2025 Sioux Falls Skyforce Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/Sioux-Falls-Skyforce/6/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
Larsson has represented Sweden at the under-16, under-18, and senior levels, including averaging 6.3 points in [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] qualifiers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pelle Larsson|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/75037/pelle-larsson|website=Proballers.com|access-date=2 February 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|first=Bruce|last=Pascoe|title=Arizona's Pelle Larsson wraps up Swedish national team experience with win|url=https://tucson.com/sports/arizonawildcats/basketball/pascoe/arizonas-pelle-larsson-wraps-up-swedish-national-team-experience-with-win/article_281be43a-28b3-11ed-a391-9b12a41a66d9.html|newspaper=[[Arizona Daily Star]]|date=30 August 2022|access-date=2 February 2025|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

Larsson played for [[Sweden men's national basketball team|Sweden]] at the [[EuroBasket 2025]], averaging 18.8 points and helping Sweden to advance from the group stage and reach the round of 16.<ref>{{cite web | title=Larsson leads Sweden to first EuroBasket win since 2013 | website=FIBA Basketball | date=August 30, 2025| url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-eurobasket-2025/news/larsson-leads-sweden-to-first-eurobasket-win-since-2013 | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>
